content.user_title: Fix Motion Performance in UI Animation
content.value_statement: Poor animation choices can cause janky interfaces and expensive rendering work. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused rules for reviewing and improving motion.
actual_capabilities: Reviews UI animation work against documented performance rules.
Identifies risky layout, paint, scroll, and filter animation patterns.
Recommends transform, opacity, batching, FLIP, and visibility-based approaches.
Guides use of existing animation stacks without unnecessary library migration.
Produces actionable review notes with violations, impact, and concrete fixes.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not benchmark runtime performance by itself.
It depends on the user supplying relevant animation code or design context.
It does not replace browser profiling for complex production issues.
It avoids library migration unless the user explicitly requests it.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check animation changes for layout reads, paint-heavy effects, scroll polling, and unsafe library mixing.

use_cases.title: Improve a Janky Component
use_cases.description: Find lower-cost motion techniques for components that feel slow during interaction or navigation.

use_cases.title: Set Motion Guardrails
use_cases.description: Apply consistent animation performance rules before a team builds new UI patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Basic Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fixing-motion-performance for this UI animation work. Flag risky motion choices and suggest direct fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file with fixing-motion-performance. List violations, explain impact, and suggest code-level changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a component or stylesheet.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Jank
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this interaction for animation jank. Prioritize layout, scroll, paint, layer, and filter problems.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Motion Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fixing-motion-performance to redesign this motion approach within the existing stack. Preserve intent and reduce rendering cost.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactor of complex UI motion.

output_examples.input: Review a card hover animation that changes width, box shadow, and blur on every frame.
output_examples.output: The review flags continuous layout and paint work, explains the performance cost, and recommends transform, opacity, and smaller one-time effects.

output_examples.input: Improve a scroll reveal that listens to scroll events and reads element positions repeatedly.
output_examples.output: The response recommends IntersectionObserver or scroll timelines, pausing off-screen work, and avoiding repeated layout reads.

output_examples.input: Assess a component that mixes Motion layout animations with manual requestAnimationFrame measurement.
output_examples.output: The guidance warns about competing measurement systems and suggests one coordinated approach within the current animation library.

best_practices: Provide the relevant component, stylesheet, and interaction goal for better review results.
Ask for priority ordering when multiple animation issues are possible.
Validate important changes with browser performance tools after applying recommendations.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as a substitute for real profiling on critical flows.
Do not ask it to migrate animation libraries without a clear migration goal.
Do not ignore accessibility or user motion preferences when applying performance fixes.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps review and improve frontend animations that may cause layout, paint, scroll, or layer performance issues.

faq.question: Can it fix code automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest concrete code-level fixes, but actual edits depend on the connected AI tool and user request.

faq.question: Does it support specific animation libraries?
faq.answer: It applies general rules to CSS, WAAPI, Motion, requestAnimationFrame, GSAP, and similar frontend animation stacks.

faq.question: Will it recommend replacing my animation library?
faq.answer: No. The skill says to stay within the existing stack unless the user explicitly requests migration.

faq.question: Does it measure frame rate or memory use?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and should be paired with browser profiling for measured results.

faq.question: Is this useful for design systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define repeatable motion performance rules for shared components and interaction patterns.
